name: Pregnancy-Related Pelvic Girdle Pain
summary: Pain around the sacroiliac joints and pubic symphysis in pregnancy responds to education, positions, pelvic support, activity modification and gentle exercise, and most women improve after birth.

looksLike: Posterior pelvic pain provocation (thigh thrust) test
Impact on sleep, walking and work
redFlags: Vaginal bleeding, fluid leakage or reduced baby movements
Severe headache, visual change or swelling (possible pre-eclampsia)
Fever, burning urine or a hot swollen calf
Saddle numbness or loss of bladder or bowel control
firstSteps: Screen for obstetric red flags and take a clear history.
Perform the thigh thrust and active straight leg raise tests, and a lumbar and neurological screen.
Teach positions for turning, stairs and sleeping, and fit a pelvic belt if appropriate.
selfCare: Know the signs that need the midwife

mistakes: Telling a woman that pain is normal and to wait.
Using strong manipulation or deep squats.
Neglecting sleep and fear of movement.
education: Explain that most pain improves after birth and that gentle activity is safe.
Teach positions and pelvic belt use.
